properties.name: Proof of concept (reflow2 0.87.0 on flo2.io): reasoning embedded in a traditional design works within one design when every premise is a check, requirement, capability, accepted decision or constraint; it stops at premises reflow2 gives no truth (TemporalFact, ChangeEvent, xref Resource), at design borders, and where reasoning is not attached to the structure it justifies
properties.source: a proof-of-concept agent, run by Claude in Anthony's hub session on his word "Could we do some type of proof of concept design where mathematical proofs, lines of reasoning are embedded in a traditional reflow2 design graph?" (all four cases chosen)
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-10-18 on reflow2 0.87.0 (flo2.io). No code was changed, no status set and no step confirmed.

CASE 1, A DECISION CONCLUDED BY ITS CHAIN. dec:idea-a-cross-type-near-match-is-a-note-and-only-a-same-type-one-refuses is concluded by inf:the-near-match-note-choice-stands-while-its-class-test-replaying-rung-2-passes, whose premise is the passing ver:a-near-match-across-types-or-within-reasoning-is-a-note-tests.
- A Decision CAN be a step's conclusion.
- The objection (chg:a-cross-type-near-match-is-named-as-a-layer CONTRADICTS the Decision) reads "answered" once the check opposes it.
- propagate_from on the check makes the Decision read "unsupported", so the break is VISIBLE.
GAPS:
- a TemporalFact premise reads "reflow2 computes no truth", so the measured evidence sinks a step (inf:the-near-match-note-choice-rests-on-the-rung-2-measurement-and-the-passing-class-test reads unknown);
- adding a chain to an accepted Decision replaces "accepted" with the chain's verdict, so an incomplete first chain reads as unsupported;
- a counter-argument has no record of its own, and answering one carried on a ChangeEvent reads that history as false;
- reasoning_report shows a settled Decision's `decision` text ("options, none chosen") instead of `chose`;
- the served skills disagree on whether an Inference may conclude a Decision (capture-intent vs brainstorm/AGENTS.md).

CASE 2, A REQUIREMENT'S WHY. req:a-near-match-across-types-or-within-a-line-of-reasoning-is-a-note-not-a-refusal was made GOVERNED_BY the Decision (it was missing).
- reasoning_report on the requirement says only "delivered by the roll-up" and names neither the Decision nor its chain.
- When the Decision's support breaks in a change walk, the requirements it governs are NOT named.
- The lineage vocabulary (`derived` = "technical necessity nobody asked for") does not fit "the owner's words, chosen through a Decision".

CASE 3, A WHOLE PROOF AS ONE PREMISE, ACROSS DESIGNS. A new proof design, ef749c7f6e03a853 ("Fermat test failure proves compositeness", hub member), proves the theorem: shown, 4 steps, Fermat's little theorem cited.
- In flo2-calc (0bee0c00b35845f6), an xref to that theorem is a premise of inf:the-fermat-theorem-proved-elsewhere-makes-a-failure-a-proof-of-compositeness. That is ACCEPTED.
- But the xref is a Resource with truth unknown, so the step reads unknown, although the theorem is "shown" where it lives.
- Breaking Fermat's little theorem in its own design takes its theorem to unsupported, but boundary_crossings: [], so the ripple never reaches calc, directly or through the hub.
- A claim inside a Decision (a numbered point) needs a separate requirement.
- A cited theorem is not distinguished from an axiom.

CASE 4, AN EDGE THAT IS REALLY AN ARGUMENT. req:claim-the-near-match-note-capability-satisfies-the-near-match-note-requirement is concluded by inf:the-near-match-note-capability-satisfies-its-requirement over the check, the capability and the requirement.
- It reads shown, and goes unsupported when the check is lost.
- The SATISFIES edge names the claim only in prose (its evidence), so deleting the edge or breaking the claim touches nothing else.
- The requirement premise's "delivered by the roll-up" is computed along the very edge argued for: circularity, undetected.
- In a what-if, the delivery-based truths are not recomputed.
- `satisfies` cannot set the edge's declared `evidence`.

VERDICT, the three gaps that matter most:
(1) Premises with no truth: TemporalFact, ChangeEvent and the cross-design xref all read unknown.
(2) Nothing crosses designs: neither truth nor breaking, even within one hub.
(3) Reasoning is not attached to the structure it justifies: a governed requirement's reason to exist is not read or named, and an edge's argument is prose.

These are the build inputs for req:a-choice-that-rests-on-checkable-premises-is-recorded-as-a-chain and req:a-derived-requirement-inherits-its-reasoning-from-the-decision-that-created-it (accepted 2026-10-16, unbuilt).
The live writes in reflow2's design listed above await adoption by the next reflow2 design PR. Check detect_defects on the two new opposing CONTRADICTS edges before adopting.
